Heidegger's Topologie is structurally distinct from Auerbach-Curtius rhetorical-literary topology; Dec 1958 letter disavows 'historical connotations.' Geviert is poetic-cosmic not rhetorical-argumentative
Heidegger's Erörterung is the practice of the Topologie: 'discussion (Erörterung) points to place (Ort); and place gathers in and permeates everything'
Ebbinghaus's draft-letter: erörtern = 'to carry contemplation through prescribed places (Örter/loci)' — the German verb has Aristotelian topics-tradition as its hidden genealogy

At close of GA 18 Heidegger asserts kinesis possesses both poietikon and pathetikon — conceptual track for BT's poiesis-emphasis. Pathos sidelined into Befindlichkeit/Stimmung. The restriction in conceptual form

1922 Natorp-Bericht: Heidegger characterizes phronēsis (NE VI) as Gewissen. The conceptual hinge: rhetorical-pathic register is channeled into ethical-existential register, restricting rhetoric's distinctive contribution

Heidegger's Eigentlichkeit and public-spirited rhetorical tradition 'inhabit contradictory worlds' (cabin dweller vs. Naples). 1962 Greece trip (imagined Heraclitus, never alighted on Patmos) is biographical confirmation

Closing image: Heidegger's 'paths' are paths driven through wood to carry out timber — end blind where timber has been already-made; 'deceive the traveler.' Topology-of-being appears to discover but ends where Heidegger's pre-decisions have foreclosed
VOLUME-FRAMING DISAGREEMENT (= VT1): Pöggeler's restriction-thesis vs. Gross's centrality-thesis. Volume opens with Gross, closes with Pöggeler

Pöggeler's premise that Heidegger 'restricted crucial dimensions of Aristotle's Rhetoric' directly undermines Hyde's reading of BT §§54-60 as 'primordial and emotional form of epideictic rhetoric'. Pöggeler reads BT conscience-block as where rhetoric is LOST
Pöggeler's reading of GA 18 as bounded philological episode contrasts with Kisiel's reading as genesis of 'rhetorical protopolitics' with continuous afterlife

Pöggeler agrees with Michalski's philological framing of GA 18 but RESTRICTS the import: for Michalski philological orientation is methodologically sustaining; for Pöggeler it's part of what makes Marburg engagement bounded

Pöggeler agrees with Gadamer's late acknowledgment that hermeneutics had older roots in rhetoric tradition; grounds broader claim that 'even when hidden, Heidegger touches rhetorical tradition again and again'
VT9: Pöggeler reads BT §29 (= BT 178 / GA 18 110) as RESTRICTIVE rather than constitutive. Hyde, Struever, Gross, Kisiel read this passage as load-bearing positive evidence
Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens (1947) is where 'topology of being' is introduced; dwelling-place (Ortschaft) of essence; thoughtful poetics. 1947 publication is temporal pivot of essay

Heidegger's own self-interpretation: 'I use the term topology quite literally: the speaking of place; that is, thinking the truth (Entbergen des Sichverbergens) of being. In using this term I was not aware of the historical connotations you have suggested.' Heidegger explicitly disavows rhetorical-historical genealogy

BT §29 reads Aristotle's Rhetoric as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness'; Pöggeler reads as moment of restriction. The Aristotelian pathē of fear (Rhet. II.5) are absorbed into Befindlichkeit as mood-structure
Letter on Humanism (1947) is the post-rhetorical document: polemic against 'dictatorship of publicness' (Öffentlichkeit), against humanism's Aristotle, against Vico/Renaissance
1922 Natorp-Bericht: Heidegger characterizes phronēsis (NE VI) as Gewissen — conceptual hinge channeling rhetorical-pathic into BT existential-ethical register

Heidegger's SS 1924 lecture (originally announced as 'Aristotle: Rhetoric', renamed 'Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy') presupposes Aristotelian classification of rhetoric under topics within practical philosophy. Rename is evidence of restriction

Vico's New Science / De nostris temporis studiorum ratione reverses Cartesian methods via topical inventio; Heidegger 'in conversation with Pöggeler would not reconsider a thinker like Vico' — judgment fixed. Biographical refusal is conclusive evidence of restriction

Auerbach's Mimesis presents 'a version of Western literature and calls it a topology'; identifies guiding-words lexically extractable. Rhetorical-literary topology Pöggeler holds out as more adequate concept Heidegger's Topologie partly inhabits without acknowledging

Ijsseling: late Heidegger's truth-of-language 'adheres strictly to the ancient Greek understanding of language, as in Isocrates' panegyric on the power of speech.' Rhetorical tradition hidden but persistent
Heidegger 'failed to ask' the new-rhetoric question about justice (Perelman's La nouvelle rhétorique 1958) — though it was self-evident for Aristotle and Aquinas
